skills.name: Discussing rules at school and home

note.text: A rule states what is required, allowed or prohibited in a setting. Use clear language and explain the reason when discussing it. Distinguish must for obligation, may for permission and must not for prohibition. A respectful discussion can ask how a rule protects people or supports shared work. A rule for one setting should not be assumed to describe every household or school. Practise the dialogue in writing before speaking with a partner; this app does not assess your voice.

sections.heading: Understand the ideas
sections.text: A rule states what is required, allowed or prohibited in a setting. Use clear language and explain the reason when discussing it. Distinguish must for obligation, may for permission and must not for prohibition. A respectful discussion can ask how a rule protects people or supports shared work. A rule for one setting should not be assumed to describe every household or school. Practise the dialogue in writing before speaking with a partner; this app does not assess your voice.

sections.heading: Apply the ideas locally
sections.text: Original dialogue: Bih asks why pupils must return library books. Ayuk explains that others need to borrow them. Bih asks whether she may renew a loan. The librarian says she may request a renewal before the due date. The exchange gives a rule, a reason and a polite request rather than merely an angry command.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Identify the setting and the action before choosing a modal. When sharing a view, refer to the rule rather than insulting a person. Distinguish explaining a rule from claiming that every rule is beyond discussion. Keep requests polite and specific.

key_words.meaning: an action required in the stated setting
an action allowed in the stated setting

examples: A notice says pupils must return borrowed books.
The librarian says a pupil may ask for a renewal.
A notice says users must not tear pages.

mistake.wrong: Must return means returning is entirely optional.
mistake.right: obligation: an action required in the stated setting.
mistake.why: Must marks a requirement here, not an optional suggestion.
